themes.consensus_view: Banks agree the June Fed meeting came across as hawkish (the Fed dropped its hint that rate cuts were coming and several officials now pencil in hikes), but they split sharply on whether the Fed will actually follow through with a rate increase.

facts_agreed.claim: The June FOMC meeting was read as hawkish, with the easing bias removed from the statement and around nine of eighteen policymakers projecting at least one rate hike this year.
evidence_quotes: Nine policymakers projected hikes this year.
Bank of America expects the easing bias to be removed and does not anticipate any dissents.
The Federal Reserve meeting produced a hawkish impression
The infamous "easing bias" — which drew dissents last time — is gone from the statement
The Fed’s statement was stripped from any elements of “forward guidance” and decidedly hawkish
Markets moved to reprice expectations of a more dovish Fed under Warsh
The easing bias was gone as forward guidance was removed entirely.

facts_contested.claim: Whether the hawkish stance will translate into actual rate hikes
facts_contested.for_evidence: we are amending our Fed call and now anticipate an extended hold.
facts_contested.against_evidence: we expect the policy rate to ultimately move lower

themes.consensus_view: Banks broadly expect new Fed Chair Warsh to communicate less and offer little guidance on future rate moves, a hands-off style that leaves markets to price uncertainty on their own.

facts_agreed.claim: Warsh is shrinking the Fed's written communication, with the post-meeting statement cut to roughly 130 words.
Warsh is pulling back from telling markets where rates are headed, leaving traders without the usual hand-holding.
evidence_quotes: Warsh effectively terminated forward guidance. Any question regarding future policy decisions was deflected.
markets that have been used to the Fed’s hand-holding will have no choice

facts_contested.claim: How Warsh's first-meeting tone reads to markets
facts_contested.for_evidence: A data-dependent, centrist Warsh likely reads hawkish to those that expect this more dovish lean.
facts_contested.against_evidence: On balance we expect Warsh to attempt an impossible tightrope walk of neutrality this week.

themes.consensus_view: Most banks see a generational, multi-year boom in spending on AI data centers and chips that is still strong and broadening across companies, though one voice warns the trade is in a late, debt-fueled phase.

facts_agreed.claim: AI infrastructure demand remains intact and is spreading beyond US tech to enterprises and Asia's hardware supply chain.
evidence_quotes: AI’s rapid expansion is driving strong earnings and investment beyond US tech
Demand is not only intact but spreading across enterprises
Asia's supply chain has been one of the biggest beneficiaries of the global AI buildout.
AI increasingly appears to be one of the few categories still attracting incremental dollars.

facts_agreed.claim: AI spending will stay extremely strong into 2027, making it a powerful structural investment opportunity.
evidence_quotes: it is unequivocally clear that AI capex spend in 2027 will be extremely strong
We continue to view it as a powerful structural investment opportunity.

facts_agreed.claim: The most direct way to play AI upside is to buy the AI supply chain.
evidence_quotes: the best way to play any AI bullishness is simply to buy the AI supply chain.

facts_contested.claim: whether the AI trade is still healthy or in a dangerous late-stage mania
facts_contested.for_evidence: Demand is not only intact but spreading across enterprises
facts_contested.against_evidence: history suggests the final phase of a mania is often the most profitable and the most dangerous

themes.theme: US-Iran peace deal and Strait of Hormuz shipping normalization
themes.consensus_view: A dozen banks and newswires are all watching the Strait of Hormuz reopening and US-Iran deal as a live oil-market catalyst, but none has staked a clear directional call yet.

facts_agreed.claim: Banks and newswires broadly flag the Strait of Hormuz reopening and US-Iran peace deal as a live driver of oil supply and shipping flows.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz reopening
Strait of Hormuz shipping normalization
Strait of Hormuz energy flow normalization
Strait of Hormuz re-opening deal
US-Iran peace deal and Strait of Hormuz shipping normalization

themes.consensus_view: Banks treat the US-Iran deal as a fragile pause rather than a lasting peace, with the two desks taking a directional view both doubting it holds and the rest just flagging it as a live geopolitical risk.

facts_agreed.claim: The deal is a temporary de-escalation that does not resolve the underlying conflict, so a breakdown remains a live risk.
evidence_quotes: The US may as well have sounded the bugle retreat call and waved the white flag
We remain at a pause, not peace—with more drama likely still to come.

themes.consensus_view: Banks broadly flag Middle East and Iran conflict as a live energy supply and price risk, with two desks arguing depleted oil inventories will keep the market tight even as the Strait of Hormuz reopens, but no unified directional price call has emerged.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks reference the Middle East and Iran conflict as the central driver of energy supply and price risk in this window.
evidence_quotes: Middle East conflict energy supply shocks
US-Iran conflict energy price transmission
US-Iran conflict energy flow disruption
Iran war inflation impulse
Middle East conflict energy price shocks

facts_agreed.claim: Oil inventory buffers are depleted and remain a critical vulnerability for the energy market.
evidence_quotes: Inventory buffers are becoming more critical
the market is entering a recovery phase from a position of already depleted buffers

themes.consensus_view: Five banks reference US labor market conditions in passing but none stakes a clear directional view, with framings ranging from reaccelerating to stable to overheating-risk.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks flag US labor market conditions as a live macro subject, framing it variously as stable, reaccelerating, or carrying overheating risk without staking a primary directional call.
evidence_quotes: Reaccelerating labor market
labor market stability
Labor market stability
US labor market balance
US labor market overheating risks

themes.consensus_view: Several banks flag El Nino weather as a live risk to corn and farm crops, but only Bank of America argues the supply danger is real and merely deferred, while everyone else just mentions it without taking a directional bet.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks reference El Nino as an agricultural commodity risk this window without staking a directional view.
